figures.caption: The first glyph is loaded, but the byte store has not executed. These native Debug views share the stop before the first store.
figures.alt: Three annotated details before the first display store. The next instruction is sb t1 at offset zero from s0. Register t1 contains 3f, s0 contains the fixed address 00000000ffff0010, s2 is zero and s3 is sixteen. Both Digital Lab displays are blank with masks 00.

figures.caption: The first byte store forms zero on the right display. The pointer and counter updates have not executed yet.
figures.alt: Three annotated details at the first displayed boundary. The next instruction advances the table pointer by one byte. The left display has mask 00 and remains blank; the right display has mask 3f and shows zero with the decimal point off. Registers s2 and s3 still contain zero and sixteen.

figures.caption: The eleventh displayed boundary shows A, table entry ten. A native breakpoint condition selects this iteration.
figures.alt: Three annotated details at displayed with native breakpoint condition s2 equals ten. The next instruction advances the glyph pointer. The left display is blank with mask 00 and the right shows A with mask 77, decimal point off. Registers t1, s2 and s3 contain hexadecimal 77, decimal ten and decimal six.

figures.caption: The default range is complete before the exit sequence. The display retains F while the counters describe the end of the range.
figures.alt: Four annotated details at done before li v0 ten. The right display retains F with mask 71 and the left remains blank. Register s2 is hexadecimal 10, meaning decimal sixteen, and s3 is zero. Two full memory rows retain the sixteen glyph bytes followed by the original guard, first index zero, count sixteen and trailing guard.
